Fail-Operational Autoland-Modus

Autoland logic able to complete flare, touchdown and rollout after any single-component failure below alert height.

Why it matters

Fail-Operational Autoland-Modus matters because it supports clear communication in Advanced ATC contexts for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as ICAO Level 4, ICAO Level 5, ICAO Level 6, and EASA FCL.055.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Fail-Operational Autoland-Modus?

In this glossary, Fail-Operational Autoland-Modus refers to: Autoland logic able to complete flare, touchdown and rollout after any single-component failure below alert height.

How is Fail-Operational Autoland-Modus used in aviation?

In aviation communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Fail-Operational-Autoland-Modus aktiviert; das Flugzeug bleibt gekoppelt und rollt selbstständig aus, auch bei Fehler unter Alert-Höhe."

Why does Fail-Operational Autoland-Modus matter in aviation?

Fail-Operational Autoland-Modus matters because it supports clear communication in Advanced ATC contexts for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as ICAO Level 4, ICAO Level 5, ICAO Level 6, and EASA FCL.055.

Who uses Fail-Operational Autoland-Modus?

Fail-Operational Autoland-Modus is mainly used by Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew.

What category does Fail-Operational Autoland-Modus belong to?

In this glossary, Fail-Operational Autoland-Modus is grouped under Advanced ATC. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from ICAO Doc 9432, FAA PCG and published by Protermify Aviation as a static aviation reference page.

Definition

Autoland logic able to complete flare, touchdown and rollout after any single-component failure below alert height.

Operational example

Fail-operational autoland mode armed; aircraft will remain coupled and roll out automatically even after system fault below alert height.

Localized term

Fail-Operational Autoland-Modus

Localized example

Fail-Operational-Autoland-Modus aktiviert; das Flugzeug bleibt gekoppelt und rollt selbstständig aus, auch bei Fehler unter Alert-Höhe.
